title: You called, you shouted (10.27)
hook: you called and shouted, and broke open my deafness
tomorrow: which short prayer of his did a visiting teacher argue against?

segments.voice: That was a week from a garden to a palace: two verses, a font with his son, a window at Ostia, a request at the altar, a kind of light. Yesterday's line: the fields of memory.
screen: `THE FIELDS OF MEMORY.` → `FROM A GARDEN TO A PALACE.`

segments.voice: Earbuds in, music up, and somebody has said your name three times before it gets through. Augustine says his whole life ran like that, and after searching the palace of memory, he says who had been calling. In his Latin: vocasti et clamasti et rupisti surditatem meam. You called, and you shouted, and you broke my deafness.
screen: `YOUR NAME, THREE TIMES.` → `YOU CALLED, YOU SHOUTED.` → `YOU BROKE MY DEAFNESS.`

segments.voice: Three verbs, getting louder: called, shouted, broke. Now notice whose problem it was. He doesn't say God was quiet. He says he was deaf. In the same passage he explains: God was within, and he was outside, busy among lovely things. Rupisti, you broke: not a polite knock at the door. Deafness like his needed breaking open, and he doesn't pretend he opened it himself. Notice, too, that the call isn't new. Called, then shouted: it had been going on, and getting louder, while he was busy elsewhere. And the sentence keeps going. You flashed and shone, he says, and scattered my blindness. You breathed fragrance, and I drew breath, and now I pant for you. Each sense that kept him outside becomes a way back in. That's this week's road too. Everything Augustine went looking for, in a garden, at a font, at a window, in his own memory, had been calling him first.
screen: `CALLED, SHOUTED, BROKE.` · `THE DEAFNESS WAS HIS.` · `NOT A POLITE KNOCK.` · `EVERY SENSE, A WAY IN.` · then, large: `YOU BROKE MY DEAFNESS.`

segments.voice: Listen for the farthest sound you can hear, then the nearest, then the quiet underneath them both. Don't chase anything; let whatever breaks through, break through. If you pray, you can say his words slowly: you called, and you shouted, and you broke my deafness.
You called. Augustine's line in book ten: God called, and shouted, and broke open his deafness.
You broke my deafness: the call came first, and the hearing came after. Another week, done.

howItsDone: Catholics pray with Confessions 10.27 as a picture of grace reaching a person through the senses, and the Church honors Augustine as a saint and a Doctor of the Church.

match.prompt: three verbs, getting louder — tap the pairs.

myth: Augustine says God was silent until he finally started listening
God called and shouted, he says. the deafness was his.
the same sentence moves on from hearing to sight and smell
you shone and scattered my blindness; you breathed fragrance, and I drew breath.

fork.setup: a friend says God has never once spoken to her, so maybe there's nothing there. what's a fair thing to share from Augustine's line, without pushing?
options: Augustine says he was the deaf one, outside, while God was within.
Augustine says God speaks only to saints, not to regular people.
Augustine says if you can't hear, you must not be trying hard.
fork.reveal: Augustine doesn't say God was quiet. He says God was within and he was outside, and the call broke his deafness. That's his story, offered, not a test for anyone.

original.note: Latin, Confessions 10.27: you broke my deafness.

trapdoor: what you thought: God speaks to some people and stays silent with others.
what it means: Augustine says God called and shouted, and the deafness was his own, until the call broke through.
what a scholar hears: 'vocasti et clamasti et rupisti surditatem meam' (10.27.38), part of the 'late have I loved thee' passage, with its run through the senses.
guess: God's call breaking through Augustine's deafness
Augustine shouting to God for an answer
a bishop summoning Augustine to the priesthood

chat.says: coach called again. almost let it ring. picked up. coach just said 'take your time.' why did i cry?
options: Augustine knew it: the call kept coming until his deafness broke. Hearing a patient call can do that.
Because you waited too long. Augustine says God calls only once, so you nearly missed it.
Because it's a sign to commit. Augustine says hearing a call means you have to say yes now.
chat.meaning: Augustine says God called, shouted and broke his deafness: the call came first and kept coming. Finally hearing a patient call can land hard.

Ostia.meaning: the port of Rome, where Augustine and Monica talked
